reason: method1 returns the first element when it is NaN because comparisons with NaN are always false, so the maximum index stays 0. method2 initializes max to the first element and then only updates it when a strictly greater value is found; NaN comparisons are also false, so max remains the first finite element. Thus with an array that starts with a finite number followed by NaN, method1 returns NaN while method2 returns the finite maximum.
